newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Capital good despite downgrade - Winterthur.
newsitem.headline: Capital good despite downgrade - Winterthur.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co said its capitalisation was more than adequate to cover its insurance portfolio despite a downgrade by Moody's Investors Service to Aa2 from Aaa.
It reiterated it expected to post double-digit profit growth in 1996 and said shareholders' equity would also rise sharply.
"Winterthur is convinced that its capitalisation is more than sufficient to cover its insurance portfolio," it said in a statement.

"We see no contradiction between the ratings agencies' requirement to strengthen shareholders' equity and our policy of promoting the shareholders' interests, as the latter leads to an increase in the company's net worth in the long term," it added.

"We are expecting a double-digit growth rate in profits (in 1996) and a marked increase in shareholders' equity," it said, repeating a profit forecast first made in October and reiterated by finance director Erwin Heri this week.

Moody's said on Thursday its downgrade reflected the Winterthur Group's weakened capital structure, the quality of its earnings, and expectations that Swiss and German market liberalisations and the company's keener focus on shareholder returns would lead to a higher longer-term risk profile.
Winterthur said its management expected results to continue to develop positively, which would strengthen shareholders' equity in coming years.

"The basis for this has been laid by rigourous restructuring measures, by a sharper focusing on markets with good profit potential, by selective underwriting and by the investment income's tendency to rise," it said.
